youtube_title: The J.D. Marshall, 1911: the shipwreck off Indiana Dunes State Park
body: There's a shipwreck about 30 feet down, off the beach at Indiana Dunes State Park. The J.D. Marshall was a wooden steamer built in 1891 at South Haven, Michigan, to haul lumber; around 1910 she was rebuilt to pump sand from the lake bottom. In June 1911, anchored off the dunes near Chesterton, she sprang a leak, and the crew patched it. Early on June 11, 1911, a squall blew in from the west; the patch failed and the ship rolled over. Four of her crew were lost. Decades later, salvagers raised the wreck and tried to haul it away, and it ended up back on the bottom. Her propeller now sits beside the park's beach pavilion, and in 2013 the wreck became Indiana's first underwater nature preserve.
